meta.title: The Path to the Bird Hide
meta.textType: story: a trip to the nature park, with a trail map

paragraphs: On Saturday, November twenty-eighth, the Explorers came to the nature park by bus with Teacher Kim. Ranger Mark met them at the gate, under a wooden sign that said "Nature Park." "Welcome," he said. "This is a national park, so the wildlife is safe here." Then a loudspeaker made a noise. "Good morning, visitors," it said. "The bird walk starts at ten o'clock at the main gate." "It takes two hours, so please stay on the path."

Ranger Mark held up a trail map on a board. The map had a key, and Lily read it carefully. "A green line is the main path," she said. "A roof is the bird hide, and a tent is the camping area." "The camping area is closed today," said Ranger Mark. "Where is the bird hide?" asked May. "It is at the end of the green line," said Lily. "Let's follow the green line," said Leo. Teacher Kim carried raincoats in her bag, but the sun was hot.

The group explored the trail. They crossed a small stream on a wooden bridge. Then the path went up a hill. On the hill, a woman with a wide straw hat and a camera stopped them. "Excuse me," she said. "Have you seen my friend?" "He is a tall man in a blue shirt, with a green backpack and a white cap." "I think that he went to the lake, but I cannot find him." "Perhaps the Explorers can help you," said Ranger Mark.

The group walked down to the lake with the woman. At the lake, Mia looked around with her binoculars. "I can see a tall man in a blue shirt," she said. "He has a green backpack and a white cap." "That is my friend!" said the woman. The children took her to him. "Thank you," said the woman. "I am sure that you will see a lot of birds today."

The bird hide was a small wooden house with a long window. Everybody sat on a bench and spoke quietly. "A kingfisher comes here every day at about five past eleven," said Ranger Mark. "I hope that it comes today." "I hope that it will, too," whispered Leo. Mia looked at her guidebook. "It says that the kingfisher is a local bird," she said. At five past eleven, a blue and orange kingfisher landed on a branch above the water. Everybody sat very still.
text.summary: The Explorers walk to the bird hide with Ranger Mark and a trail map. On the way they help a woman to find her friend, and in the hide they wait quietly for a kingfisher.
